mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 0.5% compresses discount rates for equity valuations, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days through reduced cost of capital for corporate earnings.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS < 0.5% (t-test p>0.05 vs. zero).

mechanism_narrative: Unemployment rate exceeding 7.0% for two consecutive months signals labor market deterioration, reducing consumer spending and causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of months when UNRATE > 7.0 (t-test p>0.05 vs. zero).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in residential investment (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) indicate housing market contraction, triggering broader economic slowdown and negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: Rank IC < 0.05 between joint RSAFS/HOUST decline and SPX 60-day returns over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Declining industrial production (INDPRO < 105.0) combined with rising unemployment (UNRATE > 7.0) defines economic contraction, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days through reduced corporate activity.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods meeting INDPRO < 105.0 and UNRATE > 7.0.

mechanism_narrative: Strong quarterly GDP growth (GDPC1 > 1.5% annualized) signals robust economic expansion, supporting corporate earnings and driving positive S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of quarters with GDPC1 growth > 1.5% (t-test p>0.05 vs. zero).

mechanism_narrative: CPIAUCSL exceeding 215.0 for two consecutive months signals accelerating inflation, prompting Fed tightening and negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of months when CPIAUCSL > 215.0 (t-test p>0.05 vs. zero).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous unemployment rate increase (UNRATE > 7.0) and non-farm payrolls decline (PAYEMS < 135000.0) indicate severe labor market contraction, reducing consumer spending and causing negative SPX returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: Rank IC < 0.05 between joint UNRATE>7.0/PAYEMS<135000.0 condition and SPX 20-day returns over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Rising industrial production (INDPRO > 106.0) combined with falling unemployment (UNRATE < 7.0) defines strong economic expansion, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days through elevated corporate activity.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods meeting INDPRO > 106.0 and UNRATE < 7.0.
